⭐Tourism Hemodialysis Experience at Krabi Nakharin Hospital⭐

My father is a CKD patient who requires routine hemodialysis. Here's the breakdown of our experience for those who are looking:
- I contacted several hospitals in Thailand's beach destinations >3 months in advance to decide on the potential place for our holiday. This hospital was the first to reply (all their responses were very prompt, typically <30 minutes).
- They have a fully functioning Dialysis Suite that divided their sessions into 3 appointment slots: 6AM, 10AM, and 2PM. We managed to book a 2PM session on a Saturday.
- Try to book as early as you can. Booking is FOC, but you will need to send a follow up email with the medical documents / blood test reports for their team's reference. They will reply with a confirmatory email upon receiving all your documents.
- Our impression during the visit: facility feels newly renovated with a clean and comfortable environment. Spacious but not too big. Not much difficulty to navigate self around.
- We first had to register at the Reception Counter near the Emergency Department. Standard procedure for registration was done (make sure to bring your passport!). Once registration was complete, a staff member accompanied us to the Dialysis Suite.
- At the Dialysis Suite, standard procedure was carried out by the Nursing team to check vital signs, weight, general assessment. All the nurses were very professional and experienced. My father was hooked to the HD machine by 2:15PM and finished by 6:20PM. He was regularly assessed in 30 minute intervals and was very comfortable throughout.
- Last but not least: PRICING! Charges were very reasonable and, most importantly, did not break the bank. We were already informed of the exact price upfront during booking and no hidden costs were charged during payment. Please be noted there is a 4% credit card fee if using any type of card payment, which we were informed too. If you would like to avoid this, then carry cash with you.

Just some other points to add for reference:
- Please do not pack your schedule too tightly if planning for an appointment on the same day. We booked the 2:00PM slot but started the dialysis session slightly later at 2:15PM. As this is a hospital, we understand that appointment times are tentative and can vary depending on the situation.
- Meals aren't provided during treatment (which is a common practice at our regular HD Centre). I'm not sure if it's because ours was the 2PM slot (after lunchtime). Please eat before you arrive and bring some light snacks with you, where necessary.
- There isn't much commercial shops around. There's a 7Eleven at a walkable distance, but apart from that there's not much else. Be prepared to hang out at the hospital if you're waiting it out. There's plenty of sofas at the lobby if you'd like to lounge.
- For Muslims, there's a musolla / prayer room at the Ground Floor to pray. Halal food joints aren't many around the area and are either mostly closed during daytime or only accepts cash. The locals at the shops aren't fluent in English either (as I think the area is less commercial compared to other parts of Krabi). Bring cash if you'd like to try and eat nearby, or just take a Grab to eat someplace else.
- For non-Muslims, there's plenty of food joints around the area that are at a walkable distance. We didn't try visiting them, but I would also suggest to carry cash if you want to eat nearby.

All in all, we've had a very good experience here and are happy that we found a reliable facility for my father to get his routine dialysis during our holiday. Thank you to the wonderful Nursing and Reception team who were very kind and professional throughout! If we were to visit Krabi again, we'd definitely utilise the services again when needed 😊

The price was slightly higher than the intake at the hospital in Kanchanaburi. But then again, this is a private hospital visit, so I find it somewhat understandable. I went home with a positive feeling and was given a note saying I could come back the next day between 6 and 8 pm. So I did that.

When I arrived, I was ushered into the examination room quite quickly and was told that it would cost 5,000-6,000 baht! to clean the wound and put a new waterproof plaster on it. Knowing that the intake, cleaning, and bandaging cost 3,500 baht the day before, I was quite perplexed. At the hospital in Kanchanaburi, I paid about 680 baht. The reason given was that there was now a more expensive doctor. I would have liked to have heard that yesterday. Fortunately, I had the bill from the day before. The final price has been set the same as the day before, which is really still way, way too much for removing a plaster, cleaning it, and putting on a new one. In short, this hospital leaves a sour taste in my mouth.

Terrible! I've used their services since my child was 6-7-8 years old, and it wasn't too bad then, but it's gotten much worse now. Even the nurses at the emergency room entrance look at patients disrespectfully. I have insurance and wanted to stay because I was in so much pain, but when I saw the staff, some patients wanted to go home, and the insurance would pay, but they wanted to charge extra. I refused the medication because other hospitals don't charge extra, but here they charge constantly. The sheets are stained and dirty. No wonder they have few patients. Please improve this. Put yourself in their shoes; they're not getting free treatment. 🙏🙏🙏 This is a private hospital, and the service is worse than a public hospital. I understand it's expensive, but the service is awful, especially from all the staff except the doctors, who are okay.

This large private hospital is located in a side street off Maharat Road. The hospital building is a large structure, divided into departments on each floor. There's a large covered parking lot at the back of the building and a small outdoor parking area in front.

I visited the hospital on a Friday morning in mid-February, experiencing fatigue and dizziness, symptoms similar to rhabdomyolysis. It was my first time at the hospital. The staff took my medical history before referring me to a doctor. The doctor ordered blood tests to check various values. The total cost for the day, including doctor's fees, medication, and lab tests, was approximately 5000 baht. I had insurance covering half of the cost.

Overall, it's a private hospital that isn't overcrowded. The referral process to different departments is quite efficient. The hospital's internal management is well-organized. The atmosphere inside is quiet and peaceful. The staff, including nurses and other personnel, are polite and not rude. Waiting times for examinations and other procedures aren't excessively long. However, this comes at a high cost. Parking within the hospital is relatively convenient.
My girlfriend had acute gastroenteritis, but she recovered after treatment. The hospital service was excellent.

A stingray stung my leg and I received very good and fast treatment from the hospital. Within 15 minutes I was already in the x-ray where they checked that the stinger or its parts were not left in the leg. I received the medication almost …
We were taken care of quickly and efficiently upon arrival. The staff were reassuring and respectful.
Fast and helpful.

I recommend them. The staff speak excellent English and don't pressure you to pay quickly, unlike in some other Asian hospitals. I received all the necessary documents to send to my insurance company (Chapka).
Impeccable! The medical service was very professional and attentive. They completed all the necessary paperwork for insurance reimbursement; I recommend them 100%.
The staff is friendly, and the hospital is clean. I received treatment and a prescription, and it cost about 130,000 won without travel insurance.

Tinkoff Insurance sent me here, and everything went great. The hospital is new, everything is fresh and clean. The doctors were very caring, they helped me with everything, explained everything, translated everything into English and Russian, and literally walked with me by the hand the whole time. I highly recommend it.

I was "lucky" to end up at this medical facility on the morning of January 1st with a high fever, headache, back pain, and joint pain. The doctor was alone at the time, so I had to wait about an hour and a half. Seeing that I wasn't feeling well, they put me on the couch - I even took a short nap. They took some tests and within an hour at most, they diagnosed me with Dengue Virus. Dr. PIBUN explained all the treatment and options in detail - since I sought treatment in a timely manner, there was the option of being treated at a hotel, but he recommended staying in the hospital. I listened and have never regretted it. It was a difficult couple of nights. And it was impossible to get such treatment, monitoring, and care at a hotel. The level of care was extremely high in literally everything - from daily tests and monitoring to the room/room and food. I stayed there for almost 5 full days. I thank the entire staff for my speedy recovery 🙏 p.s. I am surprised by the hospital's low rating.

Very bad experience, we came with my wife, she has a temperature and cough and I have very severe digestive problems, at the beginning they warned us that the price is around 2500thb per person, we were so sick that we signed it thinking that we would get an infusion with medicines and leave in a better condition, instead they only measured our temperature, blood pressure and prescribed medicines for which we had to pay normally at the pharmacy. When we left, they charged us 4100thb and when confronting the staff with the fact that we were paying so much money when they didn't really help us, they only checked the parameters that we had already checked ourselves at the hotel, we were told that it was for the services of a doctor, such expensive services are not even in Europe and there is a completely different approach. Horrible robbery of foreigners!!!!! We went home in the same or even worse condition than when we decided to go to the hospital because we had made the trip there. In Bali, for less money, they will come and give you an infusion directly at your accommodation and you will be fully functional the next day.

Never again!!!!!!!

text: Our insurance company contacted this hospital on January 1st at 12:00 PM. Our child had a stomach infection. We arrived in very poor condition. We were admitted quickly, no lines, and immediately given an IV and medication for vomiting and diarrhea. The symptoms subsided immediately, but by evening our temperature had risen, and we decided to stay overnight. Over the course of 24 hours, we were given four 900ml IVs. We were placed in a large room with a regular bed for our child, a sofa bed for my husband and me, a separate kitchen with a sink, kettle, and microwave, and a large shower. We were also given everything necessary for hygiene. The nurses were very helpful; they inserted the catheter very carefully and secured everything so that our child slept peacefully and nothing was damaged. They came frequently to measure our temperature, blood pressure, and blood oxygen levels. We didn't stay the next day, even though we could have; we were given medications to take home and discharged. A huge thank you to the doctors, nurses, and insurance partners of T-Bank!

My sincere thanks to the hospital, and especially Dr. Piboon, for their quick and professional help. The doctor explained everything thoroughly and prescribed excellent medications that helped immediately. The staff is incredibly friendly, and they have an assistant who can help and translate everything if needed. Best regards! :)
The service was absolutely appalling. I had to wait for insurance claim since morning, and they didn't even provide lunch. I waited for hours just to call someone to change my IV line.
The hospital is clean and not crowded. Both the nurses and doctors are lovely, from the counter to the doctor. Thank you for providing excellent service to patients.
The hospital is really great. They only speak English, but they explain everything.

The amenities in the guest rooms should be upgraded to look more international and worth the price. The sofa is torn, the mattress has a hard metal frame that causes back pain, the pillows are very thin and flat, and the blankets are very rough; they should be replaced with duvets like those in other private hospitals.
Sachet coffee is not provided in a container but placed on the refrigerator wall instead. The doctors were all very attentive. I commend the nursing assistants; when a child had a fever, they immediately took him/her to bathe or wipe him down without being asked. They continuously monitored his/her temperature until it subsided. However, the professional nurses seemed unprofessional and not as attentive to the patients as they should have been. It took a long time to get the fever medication. The nursing assistant had already finished bathing and wiping the child down before we received the medication. We had to ask for it before they were enthusiastic enough to draw it from the bottle and give it to us. They just handed us the medication without saying a word, without explaining what kind of fever reducer it was, or how many hours apart to take it. They just handed out the medication haphazardly. To get details about the medication, we had to ask. Basic things like this should be explained to the parents. There are many different medications, and parents should know what they are receiving and any side effects so they can deal with the symptoms. Improvements are needed.
Thank you to the doctors and nurses who took such good care of my wife. The price was reasonable for the service.

My children were in critical condition. They had a fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, and dehydration.
A representative from the T-Strakhovanie insurance company sent us to this …
They were incredibly professional and quick. They attended to my partner as soon as he arrived and gave him all the attention he needed and more. Everyone was very professional.
Excellent service, fast, attentive and very friendly. They were very helpful.
